pr_body:
The current `ids` option doesn't allow pinning a specific document in a
single index when searching over multiple indices. This introduces a
`documents` option, which is an array of `_id` and optional `_index`
fields to allow index-specific pins.

Closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/67855

I copied some of the `Item` code for the `MoreLikeThisQueryBuilder`: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/0700359fc2ff62a66ee5d805e85f9007f9277f8e/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/query/MoreLikeThisQueryBuilder.java#L138

and simplified it a bit. ~I haven't added any tests yet—I wanted to get
some feedback on the approach before spending more time on it.~ I'm not
a Java expert by any means, so let me know if I've committed any faux pas.
pr_title: Allow specifying index in pinned queries

@davishmcclurg sorry for the delay. I checked with the team and we're happy with this API:
* Add a new `docs` section that accepts a list of `(_index, _id)` pairs. Both index and ID must be specified.
* Only one of `ids` and `docs` can be specified, to avoid the complexity of duplicate IDs and because there's not a strong use case for mixing them.

> Do I need to update [`org.elasticsearch.xpack.core.index.query.PinnedQueryBuilder`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/063a1f2d30d041f14e982f50bfdbdb6251123b9a/x-pack/plugin/core/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/core/index/query/PinnedQueryBuilder.java#L28) as well?

Good catch -- this class belongs to the Java High-level REST Client. This is being phased out by a new, auto-generated client, but it'd be good to update it in this PR to keep it in sync. I don't think we need to account for input/ output versions in this client class.

This is a good point. Even if we disallowed wildcard expressions, we could still run into duplicates because of index aliases. For example, there could be two aliases `alias1` and `alias2` that refer to the same concrete index -- searching both these aliases with the same document ID would produce a duplicate result. For context, `term` queries on the `_index` field also accept wildcard expressions (kind of unfortunate), so it wouldn't help to switch to them. Here's a new proposal:
* Still require `docs` to include both index and ID, to keep the API as straightforward as possible
* For simplicity also reject wildcard expressions by checking `Regex#isSimpleMatchPattern`
* Make sure to use dismax to handle potential duplicates, as you currently do

I also remembered we should update the docs in `pinned-query.asciidoc` to give an example of the new parameter. Thanks for all the iterations, this turned out to be trickier than I realized at first!

review_comment: It'd be great to add a test for the tricky case you uncovered around index aliases, where the same document could match multiple pinned entries.
Is there a motivation for switching from boolean to dismax query? I think the scoring should be identical between the two.

Yeah this got a bit lost in the messy commits: 7d98d38ed853bf05db2b0d4a117c8f586c0b7b2e

I'm not entirely sure, but it seemed like `should` was combining scores in a way that caused issues when multiple `documents` clauses matched the same document.

Oh I see, I didn't realize we now allow duplicate IDs in the list. I wonder if we should just require `_index` to always be set, to keep the behavior as simple as possible. I can't think of a use case for mixing both ID-only with ID-plus-index items -- it seems like you'd always want one or the other?

I'm not sure of a use case either. I was thinking someone might want a specific document (`_index` and `_id`) as the top result and then documents with the same id in other indices after that. If that doesn't seem helpful, requiring `_index` sounds ok to me too.
